Topic: 001 – School, Community and Teacher

Triangle components

These are three component of a triangle
      School
      Community
      Teacher
These components have equal importance in a triangle. If any one of them is missing, the triangle
will not be complete. For a proper triangle, all three components have to merge together.
Relationship among school, teacher and community
If school and teacher work but community does not exist the triangle does not stand, if school
and community are in harmony with one another and teachers are not collaborating with both,
again we do not have good educational results. So, for good educational standards and to
meeting the targets and goals, we need the collaboration of all three components.
Pillars of the society
School, community and teacher are independent pillars of a society and a nation depends on how
the schools are functioning with cooperation and understanding of the community and how the
teachers are playing an important role by looking at the standard set by the school.
School as part in in the community
School is an important part of the community, it is not a mere building, and schools have to a lot
to do to serve the community. Similarly community contributes a lot to school. Communities
combine their practices, resources, and perspectives to form a shared knowledge base that

informs their practice. Members of a community of practice have a common sense of purpose
and a real need to know what the others know. So, all these depend on each other.

Topic: 002 – The Relations between school and home
   
      School is the second home for a child. It has its own culture, its name and its
       identity.
      School is the second home for a child. It has its own culture, its name and its
       identity.
      Children come from a home, which is a part of a community, with deep rooted
       norms of culture and behaviors. It also has its own identity.

School is the second home for a child. It has its own culture, name and identity. A child comes
from a home which is a part of a community. School has also its own identity. School brings
vision for us. It is said that 99% people consider school as a second home. They feel that the
days spent in school were the best one in their lives.
School as identity
School has not only the building but also a name, culture and identity. Parents hold an opinion
about the school, whether government or private. School has its own culture, good or bad, it
depends how the school authority conducts it, how the community visualize the school in a
particular area and how the teachers contribute to the identity and culture of the school. A child
comes from home holding a specific culture and adjusts him with the school environment.

Topic: 003 – The Relations between school and home
      A child needs a familiar set up to settle in the new environment of school which
       respects his identity and home culture and identity to which they belong.
Different background
The culture of a society has deep roots and the school and home are part of that society. The
child has a certain culture at home, he goes to school and figures out that the school has also
some norms and routines; at playground, he learns that different children come from different
homes and each has his own home culture.

Question 1:
       Write few strategies which help you to build parents- teacher relationships?
Answer:
Children spend a large part of the day with their teachers. Teachers and children form an important bond during the school year, and children often look to their teachers as mentors and confidants. As a parent, it is important for you to have a strong parent-teacher relationship in order to help your child succeed as well as monitor their progress and development.
Here are some techniques to help you develop that relationship:
    1) Communication:
Communicate with your child's teacher at the beginning of the school year and throughout the school year. This can be done through a friendly email where you introduce yourself and tell them a little about your child. You can let the teacher know that you would appreciate feedback on your child's progress. This will show the teacher from the start that you want to play a role in your child's education.

    2) Let the teacher know if there is something happen at home:
Teachers have no way of knowing the personal problems that are taking place in a child's life. Perhaps the child's parents are divorcing and the child is reacting by acting out at school. If you are a parent, the best thing you can do is prevent the problem and inform the child's teacher. A teacher can recommend strategies for your child to better cope with this difficult situation and will be more understanding if they see certain behaviors.

    3) Ask teacher for guidelines:
 If your child is struggling to understand a concept and you are having trouble explaining it or helping them with their homework, talk to the teacher for tactics. Maybe your child needs one-on-one time with their teacher in the form of tutoring or maybe your teacher can give your child extra exercises to practice at home.

    4) Make sure your child has a proper routine:
When your kids come home from school, set aside homework time and put away technology. You can talk to your child's teachers about strategies to ensure your child completes his work effectively.
    5) Read everything that teachers sent at home:
Go through your child's backpack with them to see what assignments and homework they have to complete. A forgetful young child might forget homework so when they get home they should empty their bag and see what they have to work on overnight.
    6) Attend meetings:
During Corona, this can be done on Zoom app about your child's efforts, interests, strengths and challenges. Don't just ask about their grades, ask how they are doing socially and developmentally. You can discuss what goals you and your child want to achieve during the year.

Question 2:
         In your opinion, which leadership style is best to develop motivations among teachers?
Answer:
     The ability or skill to lead a group of peoples in an institute or organization.
Following are the different types of leadership styles:
    • Autocratic leadership
    • Democratic leadership
    • Transactional leadership
    • Transformational leadership
    • Laissez- faire leadership
    • Strategic leadership
    • Coach style leadership
    • Bureaucratic leadership
Among all of the leadership style, transformational leadership style is best to develop motivation among teachers because this kind of leadership always focuses on transformation and improvement of functions and capabilities. There may be tasks and schedules assigned, and leaders who follow this style may ask employees to constantly push their boundaries. Most growth oriented companies tend to adopt this kind of leadership style.
Burns (1978) understanding of transformational leadership showed that this theory differs fundamentally from other leadership theories in its orientation to a long term vision, focusing on the development of teacher’s motivation and thereby transforming teachers into leaders and moral agents. By following the literature research related to the results of leadership on the performance of educational institutions, it can be concluded about the high productivity of transformational leadership, which entails a change in the culture of the organization for the sake of its effectiveness and efficiency.
With a collaborative approach, transformational leaders empower their school teachers to have a say in decision making processes and enable joint goal setting. Through role modeling, these leaders create a culture of innovation and improvement and a shared sense of purpose. This creates the foundation for growth and success.
Transformational leaders are able to influence school outcomes by outlining high performance expectations, developing teachers through support, building productive relationships, and providing instructional support.
According to researcher Bernard Bass, the four attributes of transformational leadership are defined as idealized influence, inspirational motivation, intellectual stimulation, and individualized consideration.
Transformational leaders inspire trust, admiration, loyalty, and respect which inspires teacher motivation, morale, and performance. The influence of transformational leaders has been described as creating feelings. Transformational leaders are able to monitor and manage not only their own emotions, but also the emotions of others. This gives them the ability to charge their teams and drive success.
Studies have shown that transformational leadership has a direct effect on teacher performance, teacher taking steps to improve classroom practice. Findings also show that transformational leadership increases teachers' job satisfaction and strengthens their commitment to professional growth. The result is better student achievement and sustained progress throughout the school system

EDU501
1. School Teacher and Community

The school teacher is a central figure in the education system, playing a key role in shaping the
future of students. Teachers not only impart academic knowledge but also contribute to students'
social, emotional, and ethical development. Their relationship with the community is crucial
because education is not just confined to the classroom but is also influenced by the broader
social environment in which the school exists.

   •   Teachers serve as role models, mentors, and often as community leaders.
   •   They bridge the gap between the home, community, and school environment, ensuring
       that students’ needs are met both academically and socially.

2. Relationship between School and Community

The relationship between the school and the community is integral to the success of
education. A strong partnership fosters mutual support, understanding, and engagement. Some
key points in this relationship include:

   •   Community Support: Communities often provide resources, support, and guidance for
       the school, and schools may offer programs that benefit the community, such as adult
       education, cultural events, or social services.
   •   Collaboration: When schools work with local organizations, businesses, and government
       bodies, students benefit from a richer, more connected learning environment.
   •   Parental Involvement: Parents and caregivers play a significant role in the community-
       school relationship, influencing students' attitudes, behaviors, and overall learning
       outcomes.

3. Definition and Types of Social Institution

A social institution is a complex, organized structure that influences and organizes the behavior
of individuals within a society. These institutions provide the framework for social order and
include:

   •   Education: Schools and universities that structure the transmission of knowledge.
   •   Family: The primary unit where individuals learn social norms and values.
   •   Religion: Institutions that influence ethical, moral, and spiritual guidance.
   •   Economy: Structures that manage resources and the production and distribution of goods.
   •   Government: Systems that create laws, policies, and maintain order.
   •   Healthcare: Institutions that promote well-being and treat illness.

These institutions interact and shape the individual's behavior and identity within society.

4. School and Culture

The school and culture are intrinsically linked, as schools both reflect and influence the culture
of the society in which they operate. Schools act as a microcosm of society, where students learn
societal norms, values, and practices.

   •   Cultural Transmission: Schools transmit the cultural knowledge, values, and traditions
       from one generation to the next.
   •   Cultural Diversity: In diverse societies, schools also serve as places where students from
       different cultural backgrounds interact, share, and learn from one another.

5. The Concept of Culture

Culture refers to the shared beliefs, practices, customs, behaviors, and values of a group of
people. It encompasses language, religion, food, music, art, and other elements that define a
society or community. Culture is learned and passed down through generations and plays a major
role in shaping the behavior, identity, and worldview of individuals within that culture.

6. Cultural Pattern

A cultural pattern refers to the recurring behaviors, practices, values, and beliefs that are
commonly shared by a group within a society. These patterns are learned through socialization
processes and help to shape the identity of a community or group. Examples include:

   •   Rituals: Regular, structured behaviors in cultural practices, like festivals, weddings, or
       religious ceremonies.
   •   Norms: Accepted standards or rules of behavior, such as dress codes or manners.
   •   Values: Core beliefs and priorities that guide behavior, such as respect for elders or the
       importance of education.

7. The Working Context of Pakistani Teachers

The working context of Pakistani teachers includes a range of challenges and opportunities
specific to the Pakistani education system. Key factors influencing teachers' work include:

   •   Classroom Environment: Often overcrowded, with a shortage of resources.
   •   Curriculum: Teachers must deliver a standardized curriculum, but are also required to
       adapt it to local contexts and needs.
   •   Socioeconomic Factors: Many teachers face challenges related to socioeconomic
       disparities, with some students coming from impoverished backgrounds.
   •   Cultural Expectations: Teachers in Pakistan must navigate cultural norms around
       gender, class, and religion, which impact both the teaching and learning environment.

8. Leadership Role

In the context of education, the leadership role refers to the capacity of school leaders
(principals, headteachers, etc.) to guide and inspire both teachers and students. Effective
educational leaders:

   •   Foster a supportive and positive school climate.
   •   Encourage professional development among teachers.
   •   Facilitate communication between the school, students, and parents.
   •   Make strategic decisions that ensure the school’s mission and goals are achieved.

9. Level of Social Interaction

Social interaction refers to the ways in which individuals within a society engage with one
another. In schools, this interaction occurs at multiple levels:

   •   Student-to-Student: Peer relationships, friendships, and group dynamics.
   •   Teacher-to-Student: Educational interactions, mentoring, and classroom discipline.
   •   Teacher-to-Teacher: Collaboration on teaching practices, sharing resources, and
       supporting professional development.
   •   Parent-to-School: Parents interact with teachers and school administration to support
       student learning and address concerns.

Topic: 001 – School, Community and Teacher

Triangle components

These are three component of a triangle
      School
      Community
      Teacher
These components have equal importance in a triangle. If any one of them is missing, the triangle
will not be complete. For a proper triangle, all three components have to merge together.
Relationship among school, teacher and community
If school and teacher work but community does not exist the triangle does not stand, if school
and community are in harmony with one another and teachers are not collaborating with both,
again we do not have good educational results. So, for good educational standards and to
meeting the targets and goals, we need the collaboration of all three components.
Pillars of the society
School, community and teacher are independent pillars of a society and a nation depends on how
the schools are functioning with cooperation and understanding of the community and how the
teachers are playing an important role by looking at the standard set by the school.
School as part in in the community
School is an important part of the community, it is not a mere building, and schools have to a lot
to do to serve the community. Similarly community contributes a lot to school. Communities
combine their practices, resources, and perspectives to form a shared knowledge base that

informs their practice. Members of a community of practice have a common sense of purpose
and a real need to know what the others know. So, all these depend on each other.

Topic: 002 – The Relations between school and home

School is the second home for a child. It has its own culture, name and identity. A child comes
from a home which is a part of a community. School has also its own identity. School brings
vision for us. It is said that 99% people consider school as a second home. They feel that the
days spent in school were the best one in theirlives.
School as identity
School has not only the building but also a name, culture and identity. Parents hold an opinion
about the school, whether government or private. School has its own culture, good or bad, it
depends how the school authority conducts it, how the community visualize the school in a
particular area and how the teachers contribute to the identity and culture of the school. A child
comes from home holding a specific culture and adjusts him with the school environment.

Topic: 003 – The Relations between school and home
      A child needs a familiar set up to settle in the new environment of school which
       respects his identity and home culture and identity to which they belong.
Different background
The culture of a society has deep roots and theschool and home are part of that society. The
child has a certain culture at home, he goes to school and figures out that the school has also
some norms and routines; at playground, he learns that different children come from different
homes and each has his own home culture.

Community & teacher help the child
Thus, it is a difficult task, for the child, to become familiar with all three different cultures.
However, the community members,school staff and teachers can help the children to address
three different culturesissues. They can generate a friendly environment and sense of attachment
and may instigate    respect and harmony amongthe home,school and the community culture.
This will imply a positive impact on the child‘s growth. So, educating a child is a partnership
between home and school, and that connection must remain clear and strong to monitor progress
and take action when there are problems.

Topic: 004 – The Teacher‟s Role

The teacher‟s role is to:
          Develop an understanding of the student‟s culture and communities
          Value their student‟s culture
          Respect their students families
   Referebce: McCaleb,PS (1994)Building Communities of learners,
   USA: Lawrence Erbaum associates

So, it is the responsibility of the teacher to understand the culture and community fromwhich the
students are coming from. It is not an easy task for a teacher to know the culture, community and
the home culture of each and every student; however the teachers should do it. If the teacher does
not know the culture and community of the students, she may misunderstand the situation. The
teacher‘s role is not only to know the culture but also to understand the traditions and value their
culture.We need to learn that other people who have different culture, can also Have good
values, norms and traditions. As sometimes we think that whatever we do, is best. Similarly, we
think that our culture is best or superior to others. Weshould give space to others.
Teacher as a role model
The teacher is the role model for students and thus should respect, value and appreciate the
culture of each and every student and mustalways give positive remark about the culture,
whatever the culture is.

Example
For example if the student say it is my culture that I need to shake hands with my elders, the
teacher must appreciate that, this will be a very kind gesture, that the teacher may say, ―O fine,
that‘s wonderful, I think this is very interesting‖. These are all positive statements, statement
which pride the students. Students must love that behavior and they would respect their teachers,
along with that teacher must respect the family of the students irrespective of their status and
educational background.
